cover.title: Nadine Sierra
cover.subtitle: soprano
cover.calloutLabel: A note from CEO of Vivo Performing Arts
cover.pressQuote: Sierra was luscious, lovely and free throughout her range—daring to glory in her sound, she touched the operatic firmament. The applause went on and on. The New York Times

sections.title: Welcome
sections.quote: Praised for her vocal beauty, seamless technique, and abundant musicality, Nadine Sierra returns to Boston Lyric Opera for a special one-night-only recital—the soprano who has taken the Met, La Scala, and Paris Opera by storm, performing alongside pianist Bryan Wagorn.
body: NADINE SIERRA soprano BRYAN WAGORN piano Praised for her vocal beauty, seamless technique, and abundant musicality, Nadine Sierra is hailed as one of the most promising young talents in opera today. After a string of successful debuts at the Metropolitan Opera, Teatro alla Scala, Paris Opera, and Staatsoper Berlin, she has become a fixture at many of the top opera houses around the world. She returns to Boston Lyric Opera, where she had early career triumphs as Gilda in Rigoletto and as Tytania in A Midsummer Night's Dream, for a special one-night-only recital performance alongside pianist Bryan Wagorn. Presented by Boston Lyric Opera in association with Vivo Performing Arts.

songs.title: An die Musik
songs.composer: Franz Schubert — text by Franz von Schober

original: Du holde Kunst, in wieviel grauen Stunden,
Wo mich des Lebens wilder Kreis umstrickt,
Hast du mein Herz zu warmer Lieb entzunden,
Hast mich in eine beßre Welt entrückt!
translation: O gracious Art, in how many grey hours,
When life's fierce orbit encompassed me,
Have you kindled my heart to warm love,
Have you transported me into a better world!

original: Oft hat ein Seufzer, deiner Harf entflossen,
Ein süßer, heiliger Akkord von dir,
Den Himmel beßrer Zeiten mir erschlossen,
Du holde Kunst, ich danke dir dafür!
translation: Often a sigh, escaping from your harp,
A sweet, sacred chord of yours,
Has opened to me the heaven of better times,
O gracious Art, for that I thank you!

songs.title: The Vagabond
songs.composer: Ralph Vaughan Williams — text by Robert Louis Stevenson
songs.note: from Songs of Travel (1904). Sung in English.

original: Give to me the life I love,
Let the lave go by me,
Bed in the bush with stars to see,
Bread I dip in the river —
There's the life for a man like me,
